albums.blurb: Surprise Chef are a quintet from Melbourne, Australia who work the moodier end of instrumental jazz-funk, drawing on 1970s film scores and the kind of soul records that became hip-hop's sample bed. Education & Recreation, released in October 2022, is their third album and their first recorded for Brooklyn's Big Crown Records, the label of El Michels Affair, whose cinematic-soul lineage the band extends with punchy drums, watery electric keys, and lots of open space. All twelve tracks are instrumental.
albums.reception: The Fire Note gave the album 4 out of 5, calling it "a fresh exploratory instrumental blend of soul, funk and jazz that maximizes their excellent musicianship."

albums.blurb: Laufey is an Icelandic-Chinese singer, cellist, and guitarist who writes contemporary pop songcraft in the harmonic language of mid-century vocal jazz and bossa nova. Bewitched, released in September 2023 on AWAL, is her second album, following 2022's Everything I Know About Love, and dresses her originals — plus a cover of "Misty" — in orchestral strings and small-combo jazz arrangements.
albums.reception: Bewitched won Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album at the 66th Grammy Awards, debuted at number 23 on the Billboard 200, and set the record for the biggest debut by a jazz album in Spotify's history.

albums.blurb: Thundercat is Stephen Lee Bruner, the Los Angeles bass virtuoso who came up in Suicidal Tendencies and Erykah Badu's touring band before becoming a linchpin of Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp a Butterfly and of Flying Lotus's Brainfeeder label, which released this record. Drunk, his third album, packs 23 short songs into a single flowing suite of falsetto-led jazz-funk, with guests ranging from Kendrick Lamar, Pharrell, and Wiz Khalifa to yacht-rock elders Kenny Loggins and Michael McDonald on the single "Show You the Way."
albums.reception: Drunk reached number eight on the UK Albums Chart, holds a Metacritic score of 80, and made 2017 year-end best-albums lists at Pitchfork, The Guardian, NME, and Stereogum.
